# The same entries, one sort key per pair

This is `sortkey-clamp.qmd` with the two entries of each pair given one shared
sort key instead of two rival ones. The entries, their level paths and their
printed text are unchanged; only the keys are. Written this way the index tool
receives one key per pair, files each pair as one entry, and prints it once.

Each shared key is chosen to differ from the third-level printed text of both
entries it is written on. That constraint is the fixture's, not a rule an
author has to remember: the back-end emits a sort field only where the key
differs from the level it was written for, so a key equal to one entry's third
level and not the other's would leave the pair filing apart again — which is
the very collision this twin exists to be free of.

## One side folded, the other written folded

`Kay` is neither `gamma` nor `gamma, delta`:

[Delta]{.index entry="alpha!beta!gamma!delta" sort="alpha!beta!Kay"} and
[Gamma, delta]{.index entry="alpha!beta!gamma, delta" sort="alpha!beta!Kay"}.

## Both sides folded

`Jay` is neither `xi` nor `xi, omicron`:

[Pi]{.index entry="mu!nu!xi!omicron!pi" sort="mu!nu!Jay"} and
[Omicron, pi]{.index entry="mu!nu!xi, omicron!pi" sort="mu!nu!Jay"}.
